feature_notes: attachmentLimit = 8 files per message. attach() first takes sources.prefix(max(0, 8 - attachments.count)) so it returns before any byte is copied, then recounts free room on the main actor, appends imported.prefix(room), and deletes every already-copied file past that room with FileManager.removeItem
attach returns nil when the batch is empty, otherwise the detached Task so the caller can await or cancel

readDocument calls DiskWriter.shared.waitForQueuedWrites() first so a queued save lands before the read, filters out items where isEmptyReasoning is true, maps each remaining item through cleanedOfEmDashes, and returns data.count as the cache cost
decodeDocument(_:) is exactly readDocument(_:)?.document
importAttachment(from:) lowercases the extension and substitutes "bin" when the source has no extension
importSource: directories are skipped (fileExists with isDirectory), HEIC and HEIF are transcoded to JPEG and renamed to <basename>.jpg, every other file type is copied verbatim
Pasted image data already of UTType .png is stored as-is; any other image type is re-encoded to PNG through ImageIO before storing

transcode() requires kCGImagePropertyPixelWidth and kCGImagePropertyPixelHeight, then builds the image with kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailFromImageAlways: true, kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailWithTransform: true and kCGImageSourceThumbnailMaxPixelSize: max(width, height) so the result is full size with orientation applied; JPEG encoding passes kCGImageDestinationLossyCompressionQuality: 0.88, PNG passes an empty options dictionary

Orphan sweep: a file is removed only when it is unreferenced AND its contentModificationDate is older than Date.now.addingTimeInterval(-24 * 60 * 60), so a draft open across a relaunch keeps its files

Sweep references are collected by scanning each thread JSON as text for attachment paths (the regex allows the encoder's escaped forward slash, written as backslash-slash in JSON) and, when the text contains the literal "continuation" key, by decoding StoredContinuation with JSONDecoder.storage and taking each attachment.url.lastPathComponent

MimeType.of mapping, exact: png -> image/png, jpg and jpeg -> image/jpeg, gif -> image/gif, webp -> image/webp, heic -> image/heic, pdf -> application/pdf, json -> application/json, md and markdown -> text/markdown, default -> text/plain
DocumentPrefetch init defaults: limit 12 ready documents, costLimit 16 * 1_024 * 1_024 (16 MB), pendingLimit 24 queued requests

warm(ids:urgent:): when urgent, ids already in the queue are moved to index 0 iterating ids.reversed(); new ids are inserted at index 0 when urgent and appended otherwise; enqueueing stops once queue.count reaches pendingLimit; ids already in ready or already pending are skipped
A single detached utility worker drains the queue; it is stored in state.worker and cleared inside next() when the queue empties, and next() flushes queue and pending entirely if Task.isCancelled
Every Request carries a fresh token UUID and the decoded result is stored only if state.pending[id] still equals that token, so take() or forget() invalidates an in-flight decode
take(id) is a consuming read: it clears pending[id], removes the id from the queue and returns ready.removeValue(for: id); forget(id) is take(id) with the result discarded
DiskWriter.encodeAndWrite coalesces writes: if a value was already pending for that URL only the snapshot is replaced and no second queue hop is scheduled, so a backlog never writes stale documents
writeSynchronously clears the pending entry for that URL then does queue.sync

deleteDocuments(ids) returns early on an empty array, forgets each prefetch entry, and performs one DiskWriter.removeSynchronously([URL]) hop that also clears pending saves for those URLs so a deleted thread cannot be resurrected by a queued save

files.purpose: Implements daily AI coding token spend accounting: TokenSpendTracker turns cumulative provider counters into per-event deltas, the @MainActor @Observable TokenLedger merges live per-day spend with a once-per-process tail scan of local Codex rollout JSONL files using per-rollout provenance so the same usage is never counted twice, and TokenActivityGrid lays out the year-long contribution heatmap shown at the top of Settings, General.

Days still in the future stay in the grid as cells so the year keeps its shape; tomorrow is published so the canvas can tell a quiet day from one not yet here
maxValue is the max across all cell values and drives the heatmap color scale

feature_notes: TokenSpendTracker.spend(total:before:): when unseeded it sets seeded = true and lastTotal = max(0, min(total, before)); every call returns max(0, total - lastTotal) and then sets lastTotal = max(0, total) via defer, so a counter drop from compaction or a reused session object reseeds silently and records nothing

TokenSpendTracker.seedBaseline(total:) is a no-op once seeded; otherwise it sets seeded = true and lastTotal = max(0, total) and counts nothing, for a resumed session whose first reported total is inherited history rather than spend
record(codexSpend:rolloutID:on:) returns without recording when rolloutID.isEmpty, and lowercases the id before storing it

The private record(spend:codexRollout:on:) ignores spend <= 0, adds to both state.daily[day] and dailyTotals[day], adds to state.liveCodex[identity] only for Codex, and schedules at most one debounced save

The live save debounce is exactly Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2)); the task clears liveSave then calls LiveSpendStateStore.save(state). flushLiveSpend cancels the pending task, nils it and saves immediately, for app quit
refreshIfNeeded runs the Codex history scan exactly once per process behind didStartLoad; after that only live recording refreshes the grid
uncertainTokensThisYear sums legacyDaily values whose key has the prefix String(format: "%04d-", Calendar.current.component(.year, from: Date()))
mergedTotals starts from state.legacyDaily, then adds state.daily, then historyDaily, day by day

Scan window: a rollout file is considered only when its mtime >= (now minus historyMonths = 12 months) and mtime < launchDate; files written after launch are skipped because live recording already owns them
tailBytes = 131_072 (128 KB) is read from the end of each rollout; headBytes = 8 * 1_048_576 (8 MB) is the budget for inheritedTotal, read in 512 * 1024 byte chunks

A file's contribution is its final token_count total_tokens minus inheritedTotal(at:), floored at 0 with max(0, own), attributed to the day of that event's timestamp; a tail whose token_count line has no parsable day yields no contribution at all

inheritedTotal scans the head for the FIRST token_count line and returns max(0, total_tokens - last_token_usage.total_tokens), which is what a resumed thread carried in before its own request; last defaults to 0 when last_token_usage is absent

Only lines containing the literal "token_count" are JSON-decoded, in both the head (byte-slice search for the marker Data) and the tail (String.contains, iterating split lines reversed so the newest event wins)
The tail is decoded with String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self), lossy on purpose so one stray byte cannot throw away an intact token_count line

A cached fingerprint is reused only when both mtime == known.mtime (as timeIntervalSince1970) and size == known.size; an empty cached identity is recomputed from the path at reuse time but not written back
After the walk, fingerprints are filtered down to paths actually seen, so deleted rollouts stop contributing

reconcile(): per rollout identity, files are sorted by day descending and the settled live amount is cleared against the newest day's growth first with cleared = min(remaining, file.tokens); a live amount larger than the scanned growth leaves the rest unclaimed rather than going negative; it is recomputed from the fingerprints on every scan so repeated scans and restarts land the same numbers

LiveSpendStateStore.load folds the previous process's liveCodex into settledCodex and then clears liveCodex, so this process's own in-flight rollouts are never subtracted twice; when the file is missing it falls back to reading the v1 defaults key into legacyDaily

CodexFileFingerprint.rolloutIdentity finds the LAST UUID-shaped substring in the file name with the pattern "[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}" using options [.regularExpression, .backwards], lowercased; with no match it falls back to the full path, which then reconciles only with itself
eventDate tries an ISO8601DateFormatter with [.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds] and then one with [.withInternetDateTime], built per call because ISO8601DateFormatter is not Sendable

Grid build: rangeStart is January 1 of now's year, rangeEnd is rangeStart plus one year minus one day, tomorrow is startOfToday plus one day; leadingGap = (weekday(rangeStart) - firstWeekday + 7) % 7 and gridStart = rangeStart minus leadingGap days; cells outside [rangeStart, rangeEnd] are nil
Grid totals are collected only for days from rangeStart through startOfToday, so future days always read 0

Daily mode colors each cell by its own day total; weekly mode sums the column and writes that sum into all seven rows (nil cells get 0); cumulative mode carries a running total forward and writes it into every cell including nil ones

Month ticks: for each of 12 month offsets from rangeStart, column = (days from gridStart to max(monthStart, rangeStart)) / rows, label = monthNames[(month - 1 + 12) % 12], appended only when column < columns.count
Claude history is deliberately live-only: the type comment states its usage rows are scattered through gigabytes of JSONL, which is not a Settings-open price worth paying
